notes: The phrase title describes an editorial collection; using these phrases does not guarantee popularity, confidence, or a particular social impression.

Have (got) someone’s back is mainly US informal in the checked Cambridge entry; an explicit regional note would improve precision.
For I’ve got this, treating have + got as an idiomatic expression of present ability avoids suggesting an ordinary completed-action reading.
The casual/formal labels are the collection’s broad pedagogical categories, not exclusive linguistic-register classifications. Individual notes explicitly allow overlap.
